Core Active Vocabulary (10 items):

ability — something you can do. Example: Swimming is my best ability.
swim — to move through water. Example: I can swim well.
run — to move quickly on foot. Example: I can run five kilometres.
drive — to control a car. Example: Can you drive?
cook — to prepare food with heat. Example: I can cook well.
sing — to make music with your voice. Example: I can't sing.
dance — to move your body to music. Example: I can dance a little.
play — to take part in a game or sport. Example: I play football on Saturday.
learn — to get a new skill. Example: I am learning to cook.
practice — repeated work to improve a skill. Example: I practise the guitar every day.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• I can swim.
• I can't sing.
• Can you drive?
• I am learning to ...
• I practise every day.

Grammar focus: Can / can’t for ability.
Use can and can't for ability: I can swim but I can't dance. Ask Can you drive? Use learn and practise for progress: I am learning to cook.

Reading: read the text and answer the questions.
My abilities: I can swim, run and cook. I can't sing or dance, but I am learning. I practise the guitar every day.
Listening: listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.
A: Can you drive? B: No, I can't. A: Can you cook? B: Yes, I can cook well.
